discovery: Molecular astrophysics: establishing the physical and chemical pathways by which matter evolves from interstellar clouds to protostars and planet-forming disks

nominees.name: Ewine F. van Dishoeck
nominees.affiliation: Leiden Observatory, Leiden University, The Netherlands

subfield: Astrophysics / astrochemistry of star and planet formation
motivation: Van Dishoeck and Herbst founded quantitative molecular astrophysics. Herbst developed the ion-molecule and gas-grain reaction networks that explain how molecules, including complex organics, form in cold interstellar gas. Van Dishoeck combined molecular physics (photodissociation, excitation, radiative transfer) with observations from ground and space facilities, ALMA, Herschel and JWST among them. This made molecules precise probes of temperature, density, ionization and dynamics in forming stars and disks. Together their work showed that water, ices and organic molecules are carried from prestellar cores into planet-forming disks. It also established molecular lines as the primary diagnostic of how stars and planets form. The framework is now confirmed by systematic surveys, it underpins interpretation of every ALMA and JWST star-formation observation, and it links the physics of the interstellar medium to the chemical origins of our own Solar System.
